name: Understanding why models generalize
gist: Papers investigating the theoretical foundations that explain when and why machine learning models can successfully learn patterns from limited examples and perform well on new data.
explain: This subtheme tackles the fundamental question: why does a model trained on a finite set of examples perform well on new examples outside the training set? When you show a model 100 photographs of dogs, it learns to identify a dog from the pattern of pixels it sees. But there are infinitely many ways pixels can arrange themselves, so why does the pattern it learned apply to the 101st dog? This is not obvious. A model could have simply memorized the 100 examples, and then failed on the 101st.

The difficulty comes from the gap between two worlds: the world of training data (the 100 examples you showed the model) and the world of new data (everything the model has never seen). If training and new data come from the same underlying distribution — if both sets of photos show real dogs under normal conditions — then there is hope that patterns learned from training transfer to new data. But if the new data is different (say, only dogs wearing costumes), then what the model learned might not apply. Learning theory tries to quantify this gap and find conditions where generalization is guaranteed.

Researchers study what properties make generalization possible. They examine the size and complexity of the model (simpler models tend to generalize better because they are less likely to fit noise), the amount and diversity of training data (more data, especially data that covers edge cases, helps), and the inherent structure of the problem (some tasks are easier to learn than others). They also analyze specific learning algorithms to predict how much the performance will improve when you add more data or a more complex model, because understanding these tradeoffs tells you how much training is required. The work involves statistical tools that measure how confidently a model's behavior on training data predicts its behavior on new data.

papers.title: A Statistical Learning Perspective on Semi-dual Adversarial Neural Optimal Transport Solvers
papers.contribution: First statistical learning analysis for adversarial OT solvers providing theoretical foundation; similar bounds could extend to general OT case, opening promising future research directions.

papers.title: FACT: a first-principles alternative to the Neural Feature Ansatz for how networks learn representations
papers.contribution: Achieves greater agreement with learned features, explains why NFA holds in most settings, and captures grokking and phase transitions in learning sparse parities.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds for Out-of-distribution Generalization
papers.contribution: Shows that under RCS and empirical-RCS conditions, ERM can achieve nearly optimal error rates without knowledge of distributional parameters or domain discrepancy.

papers.title: Learning Admissible Heuristics for A*: Theory and Practice
papers.contribution: Yields heuristics with near-perfect admissibility and stronger guidance than PDB heuristics, with generalization bounds for goal-dependent heuristics based on network width/depth.

papers.title: Learning to Recall with Transformers Beyond Orthogonal Embeddings
papers.contribution: They provide explicit formulas for model storage capacity and lower bounds demonstrating that multiplicative scaling is inherent under non-orthogonal embeddings.

papers.title: Minimax Sample Complexity of Graph Neural Networks: Lower Bounds and Structural Effects
papers.contribution: Proves generalization error scales as sqrt(log d/n) for arbitrary graphs and d/log n under spectral-homophily conditions, matching empirical observations on benchmarks.

papers.title: Performative Learning Theory
papers.contribution: Proves generalization bounds under performative effects on sample, population, and both; reveals trade-offs between performatively changing the world and learning from it.

papers.title: Sample Complexity and Representation Ability of Test-time Scaling Paradigms
papers.contribution: Proves sample complexity bounds separating test-time strategies and demonstrates that self-correction enables multi-task representation without prior task knowledge.

papers.title: Statistical Consistency and Generalization of Contrastive Representation Learning
papers.contribution: Derives bounds O(1/m + 1/√n) and O(1/√m + 1/√n) explaining empirical advantages of large negative sets; extensive experiments on vision-language models validate predictions.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Schrodinger Potential Estimation in Unpaired Data Translation
papers.contribution: Establishes tight bounds on generalization ability achieving fast convergence rates up to logarithmic factors for Schrodinger potential estimation including Gaussian mixtures.

papers.title: Training-Free Determination of Network Width via Neural Tangent Kernel
papers.contribution: Our NTK-based metric effectively identifies cardinal width—the width at which generalization performance saturates—across multiple datasets and architectures.

papers.title: A Fine-Grained Understanding of Uniform Convergence for Halfspaces
papers.contribution: Proves realizable case achieves O(1/n) error while agnostic case has log-free band-wise deviations with log-log n union overhead matching lower bounds.

papers.title: A Refined Generalization Analysis for Extreme Multi-class Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning
papers.contribution: Sample complexity of O(k) where k is samples per tuple, especially strong for long-tailed distributions.

papers.title: A Solvable High-Dimensional Model Where Nonlinear Autoencoders Learn Structure Invisible to PCA While Test Loss Misaligns With Generalizatio
papers.contribution: The model demonstrates a tractable case where self-supervised test loss misaligns with representation quality—nonlinear autoencoders recover latent structure that linear methods miss despite higher reconstruction loss.

papers.title: A Theoretical Framework for Statistical Evaluability of Generative Models
papers.contribution: Shows IPMs are evaluable from finite samples but similarity-based metrics are not evaluable due to dependence on rare events.

papers.title: A theory of learning data statistics in diffusion models, from easy to hard
papers.contribution: Introduces the diffusion information exponent as a scalar invariant governing sample complexity of learning different order correlations in diffusion models.

papers.title: AI4SLT: Empirical Processes in Lean 4 for Formal Statistical Learning Theory
papers.contribution: The project establishes a reusable formal foundation for statistical learning theory and exposes implicit assumptions and missing details in standard textbooks.

papers.title: Alignment-Sensitive Minimax Rates for Spectral Algorithms with Learned Kernels
papers.contribution: Connects adaptive feature learning with ESD reduction and offers novel generalization perspective beyond traditional fixed-kernel theories.

papers.title: All ERMs Can Fail in Stochastic Convex Optimization Lower Bounds in Linear Dimension
papers.contribution: Resolves Feldman's open question and extends to approximate ERMs; provides novel generalization bounds for gradient descent scaling as Ω(√(ηT/m^1.5)).

papers.title: Almost Bayesian: Dynamics of SGD Through Singular Learning Theory
papers.contribution: SGD's local steady-state distribution is effectively a tempered Bayesian posterior accounting for local accessibility constraints.

papers.title: Biologically plausible heavy-tailed connectivity enhances generalizations on cognitive tasks in recurrent neural networks
papers.contribution: Heavy-tailed connectivity induces low-rank structure and favorable representational geometry, substantially improving generalization on cognitive tasks.

papers.title: Block-Sample MAC-Bayes Generalization Bounds
papers.contribution: Proposed MAC-Bayes bounds show promise of significantly improving PAC-Bayes tightness, with numerical examples showing finite bounds when original PAC-Bayes is vacuous.

papers.title: Branch Scaling Manifests as Implicit Architectural Regularization for Improving Generalization in Overparameterized ResNets
papers.contribution: Over-parameterized ResNets with decaying scaling factors achieve minimax-optimal generalization rates, validated on MNIST and CIFAR-100.

papers.title: Certifying Capabilities from Finite Tests: When Is It Possible?
papers.contribution: The work provides a principled framework for understanding when finite evaluation can and cannot certify capabilities, with near-optimal evaluation protocols and matching lower bounds under natural overlap conditions.

papers.title: Decomposing Out-of-Distribution Error in Conditional Flow Matching via Wasserstein Geometry
papers.contribution: Framework acts as diagnostic tool tracking generalization during training and identifies dataset-specific failure modes.

papers.title: Deep networks learn to parse uniform-depth context-free languages from local statistics
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that correlations at different scales lift local ambiguities, enabling hierarchical representations; validates predictions across convolutional and transformer architectures.

papers.title: Diffusion Models Are Statistically Optimal for Learning Low-Dimensional Multi-Modal Distributions
papers.contribution: Shows diffusion models achieve near-optimal O(eps^{-k \vee 2}) sample complexity where k is intrinsic dimension, significantly improving over prior curse-of-dimensionality bounds without smoothness or log-concavity assumptions.

papers.title: Dimension-Free Minimax Rates for Learning Pairwise Interactions in Attention-Style Models
papers.contribution: Proves dimension-free minimax rate of M^(-2β/(2β+1)) that is independent of token count, ambient dimension, or weight matrix rank, establishing fundamental efficiency of attention mechanisms.

papers.title: Directional Neural Collapse Explains Few-Shot Transfer in Self-Supervised Learning
papers.contribution: Provides geometric explanation for few-shot transfer in self-supervised learning with bounds that track practical few-shot error.

papers.title: Domain Adaptation with Adaptive $f$-Divergence: Tighter Variational Representation and Generalization Bounds
papers.contribution: Achieves more informative discrepancy estimates and consistently improves accuracy on Office-31, Office-Home, Digits, and VisDA-2017.

papers.title: Efficiently Learning Drifting Halfspaces with Massart Noise
papers.contribution: Shows Δ^{1/3}-scaling is unavoidable for low-degree polynomial tests even for random noise, indicating algorithm is essentially optimal.

papers.title: Efficiently Solving Discounted MDPs via Predictions with Unknown Prediction Errors
papers.contribution: Achieves sample complexity uniformly better than O((1-γ)^-4 N ε^-2), improving upon prior results despite not accessing prediction quality.

papers.title: Fixed Budget is No Harder Than Fixed Confidence in Best-Arm Identification up to Logarithmic Factors
papers.contribution: Show that fixed-budget is no harder than fixed-confidence up to logarithmic factors with improved sample complexity for several FB problems.

papers.title: From Generative to Episodic: Sample-Efficient Replicable Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Shows exploration is not significant barrier to replicable learning, nearly bridging gap between generative and episodic settings for sample-efficient replicable RL.

papers.title: GAAVI: Global Asymptotic Anytime Valid Inference for the Conditional Mean Function
papers.contribution: The method achieves asymptotic type-I error guarantees, power one, and optimal sample complexity while constructing function-valued confidence sequences for conditional means and contrasts.

papers.title: Generalization Bounds for Discrete Diffusion: Statistical Advantage of Masking
papers.contribution: Shows masking mitigates curse of state space cardinality; structure-aware refinements capture concentration and sparsity benefits in sequential data.

papers.title: Generalization and Scaling Laws for Mixture-of-ExpertsTransformers
papers.contribution: Results provide a transparent statistical reference point for MoE scaling, clarifying which behaviors are certified by worst-case theory versus arising from routing structure or optimization dynamics.

papers.title: Generalization of Gibbs and Langevin Monte Carlo Algorithms in the Interpolation Regime
papers.contribution: Yields nontrivial, close predictions on test error for true labeled data while maintaining correct upper bounds for random labels on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN.

papers.title: Harmful Overfitting in Sobolev Spaces
papers.contribution: Proves harmful overfitting for arbitrary p ∈ [1,∞) under label noise and sufficient regularity; generalization error bounded below by positive constant.

papers.title: High Probability Bounds for Non-Convex Stochastic Optimization with Momentum
papers.contribution: First generalization bounds for non-convex SGDM with convergence rates reaching Õ(1/n²) in low-noise regime.

papers.title: How Out-of-Distribution Detection Learning Theory Enhances Transformer: Learnability and Reliability
papers.contribution: By penalizing misclassification of outliers and strategically generating soft synthetic outliers, the derived algorithm achieves state-of-the-art OOD detection across various data formats.

papers.title: How hard is learning to cut? Trade-offs and sample complexity
papers.contribution: Establishes first lower bounds for learning-to-cut framework, showing bounds are nearly tight for neural networks and suggesting gap closed and tree size are of comparable learning difficulty.

papers.title: Implicit Regularisation in Diffusion Models: An Algorithm-Dependent Generalisation Analysis
papers.contribution: Identifies multiple sources of implicit regularization in diffusion models including early stopping, sampler discretisation, and SGD, grounded in algorithmic properties rather than model structure.

papers.title: In-Context Learning Is Provably Bayesian Inference: A Generalization Theory for Meta-Learning
papers.contribution: Analysis proves that task-mixture uncertainty vanishes exponentially with a few in-context examples, clarifying that Transformers implement optimal meta-algorithms for ICL.

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for VAEs: A Role of Encoder and Latent Variable
papers.contribution: The first information-theoretic analysis shows that VAE generalization error is bounded solely by the information complexity of the encoder and latent variables, independent of the decoder.

papers.title: Interpretability and Generalization Bounds for Learning Spatial Physics
papers.contribution: Identifies function space as critical to generalization, demonstrates that different model classes can exhibit opposing behaviors, and introduces a new cross-validation technique for measuring generalization in physical systems.

papers.title: Language Generation in the Limit: Complexity Barriers and Implications for Learning
papers.contribution: Establishes that infeasibility appears already for context-free and regular languages, showing a clear gap between theoretical possibility and computational feasibility.

papers.title: Learning Manifold Data with Flow Matching
papers.contribution: Flow-matching transformers escape the curse of dimensionality by utilizing intrinsic data structure through manifold-aware decomposition.

papers.title: Learning Partial Concept Classes and Universal Rates Under Massart Noise
papers.contribution: Provides new sample complexity bounds for PAC learning with partial concept classes and completes the characterization of universal rates under Massart noise.

papers.title: Learning in Structured Stackelberg Games
papers.contribution: Develops provably optimal online and distributional learning algorithms, with Stackelberg-Littlestone dimension tightly characterizing learning complexity, enabling the leader to learn utility-maximizing policies.

papers.title: Learning to Rank from Incomplete Rankings
papers.contribution: Provides near-optimal instance-dependent sample complexity bounds for learning from incomplete rankings under this general framework.

papers.title: Length Generalization Bounds for Transformers
papers.contribution: Establishes that length complexity is exponential for both positive C-RASP and fixed-precision transformers, proving optimality of bounds.

papers.title: Local Redundancy: An Information-Theoretic Measure of Plasticity from Synthetic Memorization
papers.contribution: Local redundancy predicts downstream performance better than existing measures and enables checkpoint selection where validation loss plateaus on continual learning and transfer tasks.

papers.title: Mitigating the Curse of Detail: Scaling Arguments for Feature Learning and Sample Complexity
papers.contribution: The proposed scale analysis reproduces known scaling exponents and makes novel predictions for complex architectures like three-layer non-linear networks, simplifying first-principle deep learning theory.

papers.title: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of (Sticky) Track-and-Stop
papers.contribution: The analysis fills the gap by establishing non-asymptotic guarantees for both algorithms.

papers.title: On Contraction of Sequential and Offset Rademacher Complexities
papers.contribution: Establishes that sequential and offset Rademacher complexities exhibit fundamentally different contraction behavior than classical Rademacher complexity, with tight characterization of when contraction is possible and its sample complexity costs.

papers.title: On the Sample Efficiency of Inverse Dynamics Models for Semi-Supervised Imitation Learning
papers.contribution: Shows IDM and behavior cloning learn the same policy in limit cases, and IDM's superior efficiency stems from fundamental statistical properties.

papers.title: On the Theory of Continual Learning with Gradient Descent for Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Provides first closed-form guarantees for forgetting in continual learning and establishes relationship between iterations, sample size, tasks, and hidden-layer width.

papers.title: Oracle-efficient Hybrid Learning with Constrained Adversaries
papers.contribution: This algorithm enables simultaneous statistical optimality and computational efficiency with applications to equilibrium computation in high-dimensional stochastic zero-sum games.

papers.title: PAC-Bayes bounds for cumulative loss in Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Non-vacuous PAC-Bayes bounds achieved on several continual learning vision problems and tight oracle bounds on linear regression, with this being the first general upper bound on learning plasticity for continual learning.

papers.title: PAC-Bayesian Reinforcement Learning Trains Generalizable Policies
papers.contribution: Provides non-vacuous generalization certificates for off-policy algorithms like Soft Actor-Critic while maintaining competitive performance.

papers.title: Provable Bounds for the Learnability of Sample-Compressible Families from Noisy Samples
papers.contribution: Provides sample complexity bounds for learnable, sample-compressible classes in arbitrary dimensions under both ell-2 norm and total variation distance.

papers.title: Provable Sample Efficiency of Curriculum Post-Training for Transformer Reasoning
papers.contribution: Proves RL finetuning with both curriculum strategies achieves high accuracy with polynomial complexity whereas non-curriculum encounters exponential bottleneck; empirical simulations support findings.

papers.title: Provably Data-driven Multiple Hyper-parameter Tuning with Structured Loss Function
papers.contribution: Provides the first general framework for guaranteeing multi-dimensional hyperparameter tuning with improved bounds for validation-loss-based approaches.

papers.title: Quantifying and Optimizing Simplicity via Polynomial Representations
papers.contribution: Effective degree is predictive of generalization across tasks and architectures, outperforming sharpness; polynomial-based simplicity regularization improves generalization in classification, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Realizable Bayes-Consistency for General Metric Losses
papers.contribution: Resolve the realizable case of open problem in metric loss learning by establishing conditions under which distribution-free learning rules achieve near-optimal risk.

papers.title: SGD-Based Knowledge Distillation with Bayesian Teachers: Theory and Guidelines
papers.contribution: Students distilled from Bayesian teachers achieve up to 4.27% higher accuracies and exhibit 30% less noise in convergence compared to deterministic teachers.

papers.title: Sample Complexity Bounds for Robust Mean Estimation with Mean-Shift Contamination
papers.contribution: Shows sample-efficient algorithm exists for multivariate mean-shift contamination under spectral conditions, with qualitatively matching lower bounds, essentially resolving open question on general distributions.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Learning with Noisy Proxy Covariates: Generalization Bounds and Distribution Regression
papers.contribution: Fast labeled sample rates recovered when proxy perturbation is controlled; distribution regression as a direct special case with analogous guarantees.

papers.title: Sharper Generalization Guarantees for Asynchronous SGD: Beyond Lipschitzness, Smoothness and Data Homogeneity
papers.contribution: Obtains optimistic bounds recovering minimax-optimal O(1/sqrt(mn)) rate; extends to non-smooth objectives with Hölder gradients and heterogeneous data settings.

papers.title: Singular Bayesian Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive predictive performance with up to 33x fewer parameters than Deep Ensembles; substantially improves OOD detection and calibration.

papers.title: Smooth Calibration Error: Uniform Convergence and Functional Gradient Analysis
papers.contribution: The framework derives conditions under which classification and calibration performances are simultaneously guaranteed with provable guarantees.

papers.title: Stability and Generalization of Nonconvex Optimization with Heavy-Tailed Noise
papers.contribution: Provides stability and generalization analysis for clipped and normalized stochastic gradient descent and their variants under heavy-tailed noise.

papers.title: Stability beyond Bounded Differences: Sharp Generalization Bounds under Finite $L_p$ Moments
papers.contribution: Derives sharp high-probability generalization bounds for EMR, transductive regression, and meta-learning without boundedness.

papers.title: Symmetries in PAC-Bayesian Learning
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical evidence that symmetric models are preferable for symmetric data beyond compact groups and invariant distributions, improving upon prior results.

papers.title: The Interplay Between Interpolation and Aggregation in Regression: Optimal Sample Complexity
papers.contribution: Prove median aggregation is strictly more powerful than proper learning; demonstrate some classes are learnable only by infinite aggregation or non-interpolating rules.

papers.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Linear Contracts
papers.contribution: Matches a lower bound from Dütting et al. (2025) up to constant factors, proving optimality and establishing uniform convergence with the same optimal sample complexity.

papers.title: The Price of Robustness: Stable Classifiers Need Overparameterization
papers.contribution: Interpolating models with p≈n parameters on n points must be unstable; substantial overparameterization necessary for high stability.

papers.title: Tight Margin-Based Generalization Bounds for Voting Classifiers over Finite Hypothesis Sets
papers.contribution: The bound is asymptotically tight in the trade-off between hypothesis set size, margin, training point fraction with margin, sample size, and failure probability.

papers.title: To Grok Grokking: Provable Grokking in Ridge Regression
papers.contribution: Provides first rigorous quantitative bounds on grokking time in terms of hyperparameters, proving grokking is consequence of specific conditions, not inherent failure mode.

papers.title: Token Sample Complexity of Attention
papers.contribution: Proves attention map converges at rate C(R)/√n for compactly supported distributions, with empirical validation on synthetic and real data showing predicted slowdown in downstream accuracy.

papers.title: Towards Understanding Generalization of Federated Adversarial Learning: Perspective of Algorithmic Stability
papers.contribution: Establishes unified theoretical framework showing stronger adversarial attacks degrade generalization, with Moreau envelope approach demonstrating efficacy in simultaneously enhancing both robustness and generalization.

papers.title: Towards a Theoretical Understanding of In-context Learning: Stability and Non-I.I.D Generalisation
papers.contribution: Reveals that token-wise prediction errors accumulate over time and can cause generalization collapse if length is unconstrained; provides theoretical guarantees for ICL generalization.

papers.title: Transformers Efficiently Perform In-Context Logistic Regression via Normalized Gradient Descent
papers.contribution: Reveals that softmax transformers can effectively implement in-context logistic regression through gradient descent; provides training convergence guarantees and out-of-distribution generalization results.

papers.title: Transformers Trained via Gradient Descent Can Provably Learn a Class of Teacher Models
papers.contribution: Proves one-layer transformers with simplified attention can recover all parameter blocks of teacher models and generalize well to out-of-distribution data.

papers.title: Understanding Behavior Cloning with Action Quantization
papers.contribution: Behavior cloning with quantized actions achieves optimal sample complexity with only polynomial horizon dependence on quantization error; characterizes when different schemes satisfy requirements.

papers.title: Understanding Generalization from Embedding Dimension and Distributional Convergence
papers.contribution: Embedding dimension dominates generalization at final layer, providing post-hoc explanation and enabling embedding-based diagnostics for trained models.

papers.title: Understanding the Performance Gap in Preference Learning: A Dichotomy of RLHF and DPO
papers.contribution: Shows RLHF, DPO, or online DPO can outperform depending on model mis-specifications; proves online DPO outperforms both when reward/policy classes are isomorphic; demonstrates RLHF advantage in sample efficiency.

papers.title: Weight-Space Learning for Certifiable Few-shot Transfer Learning
papers.contribution: Confinement to finite PEFT samples enables tighter risk certificates with non-trivial guarantees in low-shot regime.

papers.title: Why High-rank Neural Networks Generalize?: An Algebraic Framework with RKHSs
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical explanation for why high-rank neural networks generalize well and extends applicability to a wider range of realistic models.
